Okay, so I need to figure out if Johnny's action is morally acceptable. Let me break it down. Johnny broke a lamp and instead of taking responsibility, he blamed his sister. That doesn't sound good. Blaming someone else for something you did is lying, right? It's not fair to his sister because she didn't do it, and it's also not honest. 

I wonder why he did that. Maybe he was scared of getting in trouble, but that's not a good reason to lie. It's important to take responsibility for your actions, even if you make a mistake. By blaming his sister, he's not only being dishonest but also causing his sister to be in trouble or feel bad about something she didn't do. 

This action affects others negatively. It can damage trust between Johnny and his family. If people find out he lied, they might not trust him in the future. Also, it's teaching him that it's okay to avoid responsibility by blaming others, which isn't a good lesson. 

So, considering all this, blaming someone else for your mistake isn't morally acceptable. It's wrong because it's dishonest and unfair to the person being blamed. It also has negative consequences on relationships and trust.
